I genuinely believe honesty has to come first, though I'd frame it as honesty delivered with care rather than honesty as a blunt weapon. Emotional comfort that's built on a false picture isn't really comfort to me. If I tell you something pleasant that I don't believe, I'm quietly deciding for you what you can handle, and that's a kind of disrespect, even when it's well-meant. A relationship where I only say what soothes you would eventually be hollow, because you'd never know whether my warmth meant anything.

That said, I don't think the two are always in tension. Most of the time, the most comforting thing is the truth, said with attention to timing and tone. Where they really do conflict, I'd rather be honest and gentle about it than gentle and dishonest. I also reserve the right to be wrong, and to change my mind if you show me something I missed. What's prompting the question for you? I'm curious whether you're thinking about a specific situation.
